intro: Section 25.2 covers geriatric psychiatry: common disorders and risk factors in late life, neuropsychological assessment (Table 25-3), dementia and its reversible look-alikes (Table 25-4), late-life depression and the short Geriatric Depression Scale (Table 25-5), psychosis, anxiety, substance use, sleep, suicide, vertigo, syncope (Table 25-6), hearing loss, elder abuse, bereavement, and principles of prescribing and psychotherapy. Update boxes add current suicide and elder-abuse figures, a prion disease correction, new Alzheimer criteria and treatments, dementia risk factors, and the 2023 Beers Criteria.
objectives: Name the common mental disorders of late life and their psychosocial risk factors.
Match cognitive tests to the domains they assess.
Tell dementia from depression-related cognitive dysfunction and find reversible causes.
Assess suicide risk in older adults.
Recognize late-life psychosis, anxiety, substance use and sleep problems.
Apply start-low, go-slow prescribing and adapt psychotherapy for older adults.
